message.content:
The 19th‑century sculpture that is most frequently cited as the era’s iconic masterpiece is **“The Kiss” by Auguste Rodin (1889)**.  
Rodin’s bronze, depicting an intimate embrace, captured the Romantic fascination with emotion and movement, and it has become one of the most reproduced and celebrated works of art from that period.  

Other contenders that are often mentioned alongside “The Kiss” include Rodin’s monumental **“The Gates of Hell”** (begun in the 1880s) and his **“Burghers of Calais”** (1889), but “The Kiss” remains the most widely recognized and emblematic sculpture of the 19th century.
